author: EmuCore - Hub
title: ANBERNIC RG406H Review: A Worthy PS2 Handheld?
summary: Retro Dodo reviews the Anbernic RG406H against vertical and competing Android handhelds, asking whether horizontal ergonomics, setup and sixth-generation performance justify its position after the Retroid Pocket 5 arrived.

blocks.text: The RG406H is evaluated as a product family decision, not only a benchmark. Its specifications and neighboring systems lead into the horizontal controls, comfort and setup process before testing older platforms and then sixth-generation software including PS2. A final cost-to-power chapter compares the result with the RG406V, Retroid Pocket 5, Retroid Pocket Mini and Odin 2 context. That ordering captures why identical or similar silicon can feel different once screen placement, grip and market alternatives enter the decision.

The review appeared in December 2024 and contains commission links, so current prices and later firmware need fresh checking. Its sixth-generation segment covers several systems within a short window, and the public chapters do not identify every PS2 title, emulator build, renderer or difficult scene. Product comfort is also personal. Use the video to narrow form-factor questions, then confirm controls, display response, thermal stability and title-specific performance from current tests. “Worthy” here is a value judgment tied to its release market, not a compatibility rating.
